segments.text: It doesn't ask everyone.

segments.text: It asks a sample.

segments.text: The population is everyone you want to know about.

segments.text: The sample is the smaller group you actually measure.

segments.text: The population has a true mean, called a parameter.

segments.text: The sample mean, a statistic, is our best guess of it.

segments.text: But take another sample, and you get a slightly different mean.

segments.text: Every sample wobbles around the truth.

segments.text: Bigger samples wobble less, so they give better guesses.

segments.text: For a sample's standard deviation, divide by n minus one, not n.

segments.text: Here's the complete picture.
